text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- World population growth slowing
- Government praises cooperation with Prague
- Finishing date for tax reform plan still unclear
- Deutsche Post postal service to stop transporting mail by rail
- German firms still keen to invest abroad
- BSE cost German farmers 750 million marks in 1996
HANDELSBLATT
- Hoechst sells speciality chemicals unit to Clariant
- "Insider trading" to be allowed for market professionals as long as price movements are small
- Bremer Vulkan again facing collapse unless funds are found
- 28 percent of German firms have plans to move some production abroad
- DAG union plans new token strikes in pay dispute with Lufthansa
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- German and Czech politicians welcome text of bilateral declaration of reconciliation
- Tax reform plan not likely to be ready until January
- VW says it is trying to reach out-of-court settlement with GM
- Inflation at lowest level since 1990, at 1.4 percent
- East German agriculture begins to make a profit
- Trade union federation says Bonn is preventing efforts to get world trade agreement on minimum labour standards
- DAG union plans new token strikes in pay dispute with Lufthansa
- Resistance in parliament to new law on recycling old cars
- 28 percent of German firms have plans to move some production abroad
DIE WELT
- Bavarian CSU party says more talks scheduled with Prague on bilateral declaration
- Interior Minister Kanther says foreigner-based crime has explosive power
- 28 percent of German firms have plans to move some production abroad
- Inflation rate falls again
- Controversy continues over proposal to reform strike law
- Farmers learn to cope with BSE crisis
-- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 26097160
